If you like deep rock galactic then its at least worth giving rogue core a try

If you like roguelite mechanics and DRG this is the game for you!  It's going to feel very familiar if you've played DRG, but the new class abilities are a nice change and the rapid pacing make it a lot of fun!

It's not the casual exploration game that was DRG, and that's not a bad thing. The same gunplay mechanics, but in a rogue like experience - you have a limited amount of time to get in, find some upgrades, mine some resources, and move to the next stage. 

If you've played DRG, the main game loop is like a deep dive. 

If you run out of time, endless waves start spawning, and unkillable worms burst out of the wall - slowly stalking you until they grab and pull you in. You're dead - and can't be revived, unless your teammates make it to the next stage. 

Overall, it's a great game, and a good inclusion to the DRG universe.

New Update is a definite improvement, can't wait to see what is in store. It would be nice to have the option for 15 Minute runs, it can be quite a time commitment with runs lasting from 30 to 60 minutes.

First things first...
[h1]This Is a Harder Game than DRG[/h1]
[h3]If you come in thinking this is just Deep Rock Galactic 2, you will not have a good time[/h3]

This game is [b]Not[/b] about leisurely exploring cave systems and getting various minerals. This game is about ruthless efficiency in killing core spawn, navigating the mines, and completing any secondaries you can before moving on to the next level swiftly.

The initial learning curve is quite steep, with memorizing what the classes can do and getting a sense for what roguelite upgrades are available during the run. Then it is a matter of getting more efficient with your time and your ammo during missions.

If you are coming from DRG, I'd recommend getting these 2 achievements to make your initial experience easier.

[table]
[tr]
	[th]Deep For Speed[/th]
	[td]Complete Any Deep Dive Under 45 Minutes[/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
	[th]Karl Would Be Proud[/th]
	[td]Successfully complete a Hazard Level 5 mission from start to finish where no dwarf goes down and without ordering a resupply[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]

Once you are over the hump, there is a lot of fun to be had here with brand new weapons and abilities. As well as everchanging roguelite upgrades to make each run unique and potentially discovering some incredibly powerful interactions.

[b]Fully auto, 8 round mag, DRG Engineer's 40mm Deepcore Grenade launcher[/b]

DRG Rogue Core is a fun, fast paced 45+ minutes session experience with fun, varied gun play, elemental damage type synergies and build potential. The game can be paused when playing solo.

I will update this review as EA updates are released.

[Update 1]  The Timer has been Updated to convey more detailed information, a welcome addition, as are the new weapons: 

-The Sludge Pump enabling crazy good crowd controll, especially with the elemental synergies between acid and poison. alt fire charges a charge shot, that when colliding with a surface or enemy explodes in many fragments covering a large area with acidic goop

-The Trident, a energie shotgun firing 3 Projectiles in a consitent, triangular spread. Indivdual shots can be aimed over long range by aiming with a corner of the crosshair. altfire charges a barage of shots that when fired don't just remove the enemies in a direction, but removes the direction itself. the projectiles have considerable traveltime and the trident itself has incredible sound design, firing it realy packs a punch.

All in all, Update 1 has been prove that the devs care about making a good game, there is the only stinker is gauntlet mode, wich is very unbalanced enemy spawn wise when playing as less than for players.

Big fan of the OG DRG and I was very excited for this version of the formula. Luckily, it's a very fun game already in its EA state. The latest patch fixed a lot of the issues I had which was with downtime waiting for teammates to gather up for upgrades, but that's no longer an issue. The random abilities are all pretty cool and it's nice how they change up the round as you collect them. This version of the game really requires much more teamwork than the OG version. I've played a few rounds with randoms and they could be pretty tough, but when I played with 3 buddies over Discord it went so much smoother. I feel like that's true for all co-op games, but it's just much more noticeable in this one over normal DRG which I mostly played with randoms. 

I'm looking forward to the updates and additions to the game, fingers crossed for some super cool boss fights.

I have over 600 hours in Deep Rock, and was very much looking forward to this.

It is early access; there will be big changes, and the first update has improved a lot of things (making upgrades less laborious, better picks and feeling less punished if you're last, more relaxed timer).

And, yes, there's a lot in here that feels weak, or poorly formed, or not fleshed out yet.

But, for me and my gaming group, this has got us all playing again.  The time pressure, the randomness, the varied classes, the special abilities, the builds, and the problems our own greed and ignorance cause; the synergies between classes.  We, and I, are loving it.

It's not Deep Rock, and won't be; I'm looking forward to more variety and changes over time, but, for me, there's a really solid change to the DRG gameplay loop, I'm thoroughly enjoying it.

I was a fan of this game, even before the recent changes. 

Given the comments and desire for change, I think that the Devs made a fantastic series of changes, addressing the desire for change but without changing the intended purpose behind those designs! Great dev-work there.
- Timer: The timer feels very necessary to me, I never felt like it was too oppressive, but the new changes, allowing you to reduce or even increase the severity of the timer is such a cool idea.
- Perks: The global perk acquisition is a GREAT change, it will help ease the time pressure as players dont need to waste time regrouping. Also the changes allow for the cooperation intended with perk selection, whilst not being as harsh if build conflict. 
Solid changes!

Oh boy. This game I thought was gonna be amazing but this has been a let down so far. I know that they can still make this game so much better than it is now. They have already been changing alot for the better such as the upgrade picking system but there is alot that does not feel great still.

First off the enemies are insanely tanky if you are unable to hit weakpoints with the only exception feeling like grenades and elemental affects. Bosses are just giant bullet sponges and I think difficulty doesn't even affect enemy health or damage as it isnt stated on the difficulty selection. The game on difficulty 3 felt easy for what was supposed to be a harder diffculty and difficulty 1 felt insane for being the easiest difficulty so i'm certain that diffculty only affects what it states in its description which is only the timer length and the bonus xp you get. I understand they were going for a rogue like feel for the game but the first game felt so approachable for its diffculty changes which made it so you could choose between a hardcore or casual experience whenever you wanted.

I think the timer is fine as it is a roguelike after all but I really think there should be some kind of way to extend your time while in a mission. Maybe make it so there are certain side missions you can complete to slow down the giant worm that shows up to kill you thus giving you a time extension. Even on the easiest difficulty the timer feels so restrictive that when you first start the game and are just trying to understand what everything does it feels like you don't have enough time to discover everything and learn about it. Maybe that is what they want from the game but it doesn't feel good at all.

The good points are the weapons and classes for sure. They weapons to me felt really good and looked really cool but again the problem is almost all of them dont do much of any damage unless you can hit weakpoints. Which leads me into the other problem which is ammo economy, oh boy does it feel horrible when you mag dump into a single grunt enemy cus you can't hit weakpoints and now you are out of ammo. Ok no big deal just call down a resupply pod and restock your ammo... There is no nitra and you cannot call in supply pods. You must now find supply pods scattered throughout the map which now turns your ammo into a very finite resource. Not to mention supply pods only give as many supplies as there are players now (1 resupply per player) which means you cant get extra ammo by playing solo and you are just as screwed in single player as well as multiplayer. There is a class that gets an ammo box but it only works once before you have to resupply it at a resupply pod.... 

Not only is your ammo a very finite resource but so is your shield now. Actually there are no shields because its now armor. Unlike the first game where you could take a bit of damage and shrug it off as long as you didn't get hit too much, you are now getting severely punished anytime you take any damage whatsoever because armor doesn't regen and can only be restored by 50% at a supply pod or at one of the very few armor boxes that also refill armor by 50%. That's right supply pods dont give health anymore and instead give you armor. They try to make up for this by there being perks that drop red sugar when enemies die under certain conditions or you get vampire which lets you get health when you melee kill an enemy. There are also more red sugar crystals in caves now which is good so I guess its not too bad. There is also a class that lets you restore your team's armor in an area but it only lets you fill it up to 50%.

There are so many cool and good ideas in this game but overall it just feels like the game is constantly trying to punish you at every corner. If you are expecting a slightly different version of Deep Rock Galactic I definitely would recommend just going back to deep rock. If you want an insanely hard version of deep rock that constantly punishes you then look no further!

Despite it being in Early Access with some bugs and glitches, I enjoy what it has so far after Update #1! 

It's exactly as they said: difficult, fast, and intense as the timer counts down (which I'm VERY glad they added an actual countdown to that), but still thrilling as you shoot Corespawn while cooperating with the group for the best choices (that now rotate instead of being strictly limited to ONLY what's on screen the first time), and better ammo/health drop points to help everyone focus on getting from point A to D (maybe) skipping B and C!

Still need more work on adding more content and bug-fixing (especially for the exercise minigames), but I say give it a shot if you're already a fan of Deep Rock Galactic AND want it to go more into that shooter-element!
